definition: Immediately before a new monthly interest period, a loan has $7,400.00 principal. You make an extra $600.00 payment applied entirely to principal, with no penalty. The nominal annual interest rate is 7.2%, and next month's interest uses annual rate/12 on opening principal. How much lower is that next month's interest? Use unrounded interest amounts and round only the final difference.
explanation: Only the extra principal changes interest. The unrounded difference is [$7,400.00 − ($7,400.00 − $600.00)] × 7.2/1200 = $600.00 × 7.2/1200, which rounds to $3.60 saved next month.
